cold_open.hook: Nasdaq down 1.84% as chip stocks crater—but Eli Lilly's up 3.2% on a jobs report that somehow argues for both a rate hike AND a cut.

markets.macro_note: Jobs beat, but inflation signals mixed—Fed has cover to move either direction, so nobody moves.

big_story.story_title: One argument for a rate hike, another for a rate cut, after blowout jobs report
big_story.angle: The jobs report was so strong it's become a Rorschach test: hawks see wage pressure, doves see no recession risk. The Fed gets to do nothing and call it data-dependent.

quick_hits.angle: Anthropic IPO prices AI valuations at a moment when the market can't decide if AI is infrastructure or tulips.
Chipotle's turnaround is operational—unit economics, pricing power, execution. Starbucks is just hoping people forget about the CEO drama.
Broadway's $1.9B season proves consumers will spend on *experiences* even as they're terrified about rates—the real consumer story nobody's talking about.
NSA using Anthropic's model for cyber ops is the first real-world government adoption—not a press release, actual classified work.

odd_thing.joke_angle: DOGE wanted to mark 2.7 million people dead at Social Security—the most efficient way to cut the deficit is apparently just declaring people don't exist.

sign_off.callback_target: the Fed's Rorschach test—we'll see which way they actually lean when the data gets *really* messy.
